newsitem.title: USA: Senate leaders seek CIA nominee's FBI files.
newsitem.headline: Senate leaders seek CIA nominee's FBI files.

text.p: Some U.S. Senate leaders are refusing to hold confirmation hearings for Anthony Lake's nomination as director of the Central Intelligence Agency unless the Federal Bureau of Investgation turns over all its files on Lake, the New York Times said Friday.
The report said the chairman of the Senate Intelligence Committee, Sen. Richard Shelby, made the demand and was backed by Majority Leader Trent Lott and other conservative Republicans.
Shelby, an Alabama Republican, told the paper the FBI's summary reports on Lake were insufficient.

The report said Lake, who was nominated to the post by President Clinton, may still be confirmed because nine Democrats and two Republicans on the 19-member intelligence committee are expected to vote for him.
